newsitem.title: UK: Britain plans ban on import and use of asbestos.
newsitem.headline: Britain plans ban on import and use of asbestos.

text.p: The government said on Wednesday it was looking for a way to ban completely the import, supply and use of asbestos, which is blamed in Britain for 3,500 deaths a year.

Environment Minister Angela Eagle told parliament she was consulting the official Health and Safety Commission about the best way to end the use of asbestos once and for all, and promised to "respond speedily to the commission's advice."

"I stress that the government is keen to see urgent action on the ban we desire, but I am also keen not to act rashly or irresponsibly," she said. "We have asked the commission to advise how, and to what timetable such a ban can be introduced."
About 3,500 people die each year in Britain from asbestos-related diseases. The figure is expected to increase in the next few decades.

The European Union has already banned the most dangerous types of asbestos, crocidolite (blue) and amosite (brown), but other types are still being used. Because asbestos illnesses have a 15-60 year latency, most deaths are result from exposure long before.
The major risk in Britain is from building materials.
